Running fleet servers showed up twice in the model picker: once live, once as "(offline - start from menubar)".

Cause: the catalog fill-in in `packages/coding-agent/extensions/hummin-local.ts` pushed every configured fleet model as an offline entry without checking `listed`, so a model that discovery had already listed live got a second entry. The remembered-models loop right after it already had that check.

Fix: skip configured ids that are already listed. One line.

Side effect: the duplicate shared the live model's `id|baseUrl` failover key and was pushed after it, so it overwrote the live model's failover chain. The live chain is kept now.

Not changed: a live server that doesn't answer `/props` and has nothing remembered still falls back to `HUMMIN_CTX` / 16384 instead of the configured window (`hummin-local.ts:485`).

Verification:
1. New test `lists a running fleet model once, not again as an offline catalog entry` in `test/hummin-local-extension.test.ts` failed before the fix (`1 failed | 5 passed`) and passes after.
2. `npx vitest run` on the 5 fleet test files (`hummin-local-extension`, `fleet-provider-ids`, `hummin-fleet-model-resolution`, `hummin-fleet-health`, `hummin-local-stream`): 33 passed.
3. `npm run check`: Biome clean (2549 files, no fixes). `tsc --noEmit` fails with 101 errors, 95 in `packages/chord` and 6 in `packages/schema`, missing modules (`react`, `ajv`) in my local install, none in `coding-agent`. The examples `tsc` and browser smoke steps didn't run after that.

No issue to link: issues are disabled on this repo.
The fix adds `if (listed.has(entry.id)) continue;` before pushing the offline catalog entry, mirroring the check already in the remembered-models loop. Now the test file:

diff --cc packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md
index 0dcad4e52,4c54742cc..bfc65a080
--- a/packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md
@@@ -4,13 -4,9 +4,14 @@@
  
  ### Added
  
 +- Fleet servers can use `"kind": "systemd"` for Linux hosts: Hummin probes the unit with `systemctl is-active` and starts or stops it with `sudo -n systemctl` (restart is stop then start). Fleet commands run through `/bin/sh` outside macOS, since NixOS has no `/bin/zsh`
 +
 +### Changed
 +
 +- Updated dependencies flagged by `npm audit`: zod is pinned to 4.6.6 for every package (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5), minimatch to 11.0.3 (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249), `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` to 0.0.81 (it reads zod through `zod/v3`), shx to 0.4.0 and `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` to 1.4.11. The `minimatch` module bundled for extensions no longer exports `makeRe` or `AST`
  - `pi update` now lists each updated package with its npm version or git commit change, for example `npm:foo 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0`, and prints `Packages are already up to date` when nothing changed. When nothing changed but an update printed a warning, for example because npm left the old version installed after resolving stale registry metadata, it prints `No packages were updated, see the warnings above` instead; in offline mode it prints `Skipped package updates (offline mode)`. `PackageManager.update()` reports each changed package as a new `result` progress event whose `message` holds that line ([#11707](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11707), [#11711](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11711))
  - Anthropic sessions now use message threads: each request sends only the new messages and the server continues from the previous reply, falling back to the full request when the conversation changed (for example after compaction or a tool list change). On by default for the `anthropic` provider on `api.anthropic.com`; set `compat.supportsMessageThreads` in `models.json` to enable it for gateways that forward the `thread` field, or to turn it off. Cache warming does not touch the session's thread ([#11545](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11545))
+ - `pi.registerMarkdownTransformer()` takes an optional `{ messageTypes }` that selects the Markdown surfaces a transformer runs on. Besides user, assistant, and thinking Markdown, transformers can now opt into `custom` (custom messages and skill blocks), `summary` (branch and compaction summaries), and `changelog` (What's New, `/changelog`, the Extension Updates notice, and the Update Available note). Without options a transformer runs on user, assistant, and thinking Markdown as before. The built-in Mermaid renderer now also draws diagrams in expanded branch and compaction summaries
  
  ### Fixed

### Added

- Added `replaceControlCharacters()` to replace runs of C0 and C1 control characters with a space
- Added `Component.capturesViewportInput`. While a component that sets it has focus, `TuiAltScreen` sends viewport keys such as PageUp/PageDown to it instead of scrolling the transcript, as it already does for focused overlays. `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, and `Editor` with open autocomplete set it ([#7629](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7629), based on [#7680](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/7680) by [@muyiyr](https://github.com/muyiyr))
- Added `getSelectPageIndex()` to compute the selection after a `tui.select.pageUp` or `tui.select.pageDown` key ([#7629](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7629), based on [#7680](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/7680) by [@muyiyr](https://github.com/muyiyr))

### Fixed

- Fixed Markdown rendering HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) as visible text ([#11710](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11710))
- Fixed `Shift+Enter` queueing a follow-up in Apple Terminal setups that send `ESC` + Return. When local native Shift detection is available (Apple Terminal, native Windows), `ProcessTerminal` now treats `ESC` + Return with Shift held as `Shift+Enter`; without Shift it remains `Alt+Enter` ([#11559](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11559))
- Fixed regular-mode `TUI` writing OSC 133 prompt markers from rendered lines to the terminal. Terminals treat `133;A` as a new shell prompt and drop the OSC 7501 program status, so the working indicator disappeared during runs. Fullscreen still uses the markers for prompt navigation and already stripped them ([#11519](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11519))
- Fixed fullscreen double-click selection splitting paths and tokens at `~`, `.`, `\`, and `+`. Word characters now match iTerm2's defaults ([#10980](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10980))
- Fixed `fuzzyMatch()` ranking a query scattered over an earlier part of the text above a contiguous match later in it. It now also scores each contiguous occurrence of the query and keeps the best alignment ([#11220](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11220), [#11296](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11296))
- Fixed `ProcessTerminal.setTitle()` writing control characters from the title, which could end the title sequence and send the rest to the terminal as escape sequences
- Fixed display math wider than the content width being wrapped row by row, which split fractions and sums apart. It now falls back to the raw LaTeX source ([#11483](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11483))
- Fixed `tui.select.pageUp` and `tui.select.pageDown` being ignored by `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, and editor autocomplete ([#7629](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7629), based on [#7680](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/7680) by [@muyiyr](https://github.com/muyiyr))
- Fixed `wrapTextWithAnsi()` starting the next line with a space when a styled word ended exactly at the wrap width, and strikethrough continuing into the right padding of wrapped lines ([#10925](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10925))
- Fixed `Markdown` styling, highlighting, and wrapping every block on each render. It now reuses the top-level blocks of its last render, so a streaming message renders only its changed last block, and a resize reuses highlighted code. Reused blocks are held weakly and dropped by `invalidate()`, which a theme change must call because `MarkdownTheme.highlightCode` results are reused until then ([#10971](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10971))
- Fixed `Text.setText()` with unchanged text dropping the wrapped lines, so renderers that set the same text on every update wrapped it again ([#10971](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10971))
- Fixed Orca terminals falling back to text for inline images. Orca is now recognized as supporting true color and hyperlinks, and Kitty images when it advertises `ORCA_IMAGE_PROTOCOL=kitty` ([#9329](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9329) by [@XRX193](https://github.com/XRX193))
- Fixed bare Markdown URLs swallowing following CJK punctuation and text; explicit Markdown links and angle autolinks are unchanged ([#10934](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10934) by [@haoqixu](https://github.com/haoqixu))
- Fixed Kitty-protocol F1-F12 shortcuts, including modified function keys, not being recognized, and F13+ and other functional keys inserting invisible private-use characters into the editor ([#11419](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11419), [#11345](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11345))
- Fixed Kitty images inside padded or colored boxes disappearing when their first row scrolled above the fullscreen viewport. Partially visible images are now cropped correctly, including beside other text
- Fixed deeply nested Markdown blockquotes producing exponentially many lines, hanging or crashing rendering once their borders exhausted the available width ([#11272](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11272))

## [1.10.0] - 2026-11-04
=======
### Breaking Changes

- `openai-completions` no longer sends `"tools": []` when a request has no tools but the conversation contains tool calls or tool results; the field is omitted. This fixes 400 errors (`tools must not be an empty array`) from vLLM 0.20+, also behind LiteLLM. Proxies that require `tools` once the history has tool calls, such as older LiteLLM versions in front of Anthropic, now reject these requests; set `compat.requiresToolsWithToolHistory: true` on those models to send the empty array again ([#11843](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11843))

### Added

- Anthropic requests with a `sessionId` (and `cacheRetention` not `"none"`) now use message threads (`message-threads-2026-08-12` beta): the server continues from the previous reply and pi sends only the new messages instead of the whole conversation. When anything earlier in the request changed, or the server can't continue the thread, the full request is sent. Token counts and prompt caching are unchanged. On by default only for the `anthropic` provider on `api.anthropic.com`; set `compat.supportsMessageThreads` to change that, for example for gateways that forward the `thread` field. Call `cleanupSessionResources(sessionId)` when a session ends to free the per-session state ([#11545](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11545))
- Added `StreamOptions.disableContinuation`, which keeps a request from using or replacing server-side continuation state such as Anthropic message threads. Set it on requests that repeat an earlier one, such as cache warming ([#11545](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11545))
- Added `@earendil-works/pi-ai/lazy-oauth` (`registerLazyOAuthFlows()`) and `@earendil-works/pi-ai/lazy-bedrock-provider` (`registerLazyBedrockProvider()`, built on the new `setBedrockProviderLoader()`) for Node bundles that split at dynamic imports: the OAuth login flows and Bedrock load through literal dynamic imports, so the bundler keeps them inside the bundle as chunks that load on first use, instead of through the variable-specifier imports that load pi-ai's own files at runtime. Nothing changes without calling them.

### Changed

- Renamed the "OpenAI Codex (legacy)" provider back to "OpenAI Codex"

### Fixed

- Fixed tool arguments for `Type.BigInt()` and `Type.Undefined()` parameters being rejected: they convert as TypeBox converted them (`"42"` and `42` to `42n`, `null` to `undefined`), now that pi-schema supports both types. `Type.Void()` still rejects every JSON argument.
- Fixed OpenCode Go Claude Haiku 5.5 failing with a 400 (`Invalid signature in thinking block ... bound to a different conversation`) after the tool list, system prompt, or earlier history changed, which left the session failing on every retry. OpenCode Go and Zen Claude 5.5 models, Opus 5, and Fable 5.1 now use per-message effort and send `thinking.block_binding: drop_block`, like the Anthropic provider ([#10954](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10954))
- Fixed Anthropic non-strict tool schemas dropping root `$defs` and `definitions`, which left property `$ref`s pointing at nothing. Claude then produced wrong arguments for such tools (common in MCP servers), for example a JSON string instead of an object, and some Anthropic-compatible gateways rejected the request outright ([#9557](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9557))
- Fixed OpenRouter rejecting requests with a 400 (`This endpoint's maximum context length is ...`) for models whose output limit is close to the context window, such as DeepSeek flash. OpenRouter counts the input with its own tokenizer, which can be several percent higher than the provider's count, and pi left only 4,096 tokens spare. pi then treated the 400 as a context overflow and compacted the session, even at around 20% of the window. The default output limit now leaves 15% of the estimated input unused, and near a full window at most 32,768 output tokens are requested ([#10497](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10497))
- Fixed Azure GPT-6 Astra, Luna, Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6.1 Terra using a 272K context window instead of the 1,050,000 tokens Azure Foundry deploys them with ([#11742](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11742))

# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Breaking Changes

- `openai-completions` no longer sends `"tools": []` when a request has no tools but the conversation contains tool calls or tool results; the field is omitted. This fixes 400 errors (`tools must not be an empty array`) from vLLM 0.20+, also behind LiteLLM. Proxies that require `tools` once the history has tool calls, such as older LiteLLM versions in front of Anthropic, now reject these requests; set `compat.requiresToolsWithToolHistory: true` on those models to send the empty array again ([#11843](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11843))

### Added

- Anthropic requests with a `sessionId` (and `cacheRetention` not `"none"`) now use message threads (`message-threads-2026-08-12` beta): the server continues from the previous reply and pi sends only the new messages instead of the whole conversation. When anything earlier in the request changed, or the server can't continue the thread, the full request is sent. Token counts and prompt caching are unchanged. On by default only for the `anthropic` provider on `api.anthropic.com`; set `compat.supportsMessageThreads` to change that, for example for gateways that forward the `thread` field. Call `cleanupSessionResources(sessionId)` when a session ends to free the per-session state ([#11545](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11545))
- Added `StreamOptions.disableContinuation`, which keeps a request from using or replacing server-side continuation state such as Anthropic message threads. Set it on requests that repeat an earlier one, such as cache warming ([#11545](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11545))
- Added `@earendil-works/pi-ai/lazy-oauth` (`registerLazyOAuthFlows()`) and `@earendil-works/pi-ai/lazy-bedrock-provider` (`registerLazyBedrockProvider()`, built on the new `setBedrockProviderLoader()`) for Node bundles that split at dynamic imports: the OAuth login flows and Bedrock load through literal dynamic imports, so the bundler keeps them inside the bundle as chunks that load on first use, instead of through the variable-specifier imports that load pi-ai's own files at runtime. Nothing changes without calling them.

### Changed

- Renamed the "OpenAI Codex (legacy)" provider back to "OpenAI Codex"

### Fixed

- Fixed tool arguments for `Type.BigInt()` and `Type.Undefined()` parameters being rejected: they convert as TypeBox converted them (`"42"` and `42` to `42n`, `null` to `undefined`), now that pi-schema supports both types. `Type.Void()` still rejects every JSON argument.
- Fixed OpenCode Go Claude Haiku 5.5 failing with a 400 (`Invalid signature in thinking block ... bound to a different conversation`) after the tool list, system prompt, or earlier history changed, which left the session failing on every retry. OpenCode Go and Zen Claude 5.5 models, Opus 5, and Fable 5.1 now use per-message effort and send `thinking.block_binding: drop_block`, like the Anthropic provider ([#10954](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10954))
- Fixed Anthropic non-strict tool schemas dropping root `$defs` and `definitions`, which left property `$ref`s pointing at nothing. Claude then produced wrong arguments for such tools (common in MCP servers), for example a JSON string instead of an object, and some Anthropic-compatible gateways rejected the request outright ([#9557](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9557))
- Fixed OpenRouter rejecting requests with a 400 (`This endpoint's maximum context length is ...`) for models whose output limit is close to the context window, such as DeepSeek flash. OpenRouter counts the input with its own tokenizer, which can be several percent higher than the provider's count, and pi left only 4,096 tokens spare. pi then treated the 400 as a context overflow and compacted the session, even at around 20% of the window. The default output limit now leaves 15% of the estimated input unused, and near a full window at most 32,768 output tokens are requested ([#10497](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10497))
- Fixed Azure GPT-6 Astra, Luna, Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6.1 Terra using a 272K context window instead of the 1,050,000 tokens Azure Foundry deploys them with ([#11742](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11742))

# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

## [1.10.0] - 2026-11-04

### Added

- Added `PipeTransport`, MCP's stdio transport over a program started by the caller through an `McpPipe` (`write`, `closeStdin`, `close`, `exited`), for example `@earendil-works/pi-env`'s `openProcess()` on another machine. `StdioTransport` and `PipeTransport` share the newline-delimited framing and the stderr tail.
- Added MCP OAuth sign-in in two halves (`@earendil-works/pi-mcp/oauth`), moved from pi's coding agent: `startMcpSignIn()` refreshes the stored tokens or returns the authorization URL, and `completeMcpSignIn()` exchanges the code later, possibly in another request with the same state store. The code comes from a loopback callback server (`listenForLoopbackSignIn()`, `waitForLoopbackSignIn()`), the application's own callback route, or a pasted redirect URL (`responseFromRedirectUrl()`). Client ID Metadata Documents (`clientMetadataDocuments`) and the client name are the caller's. Aborting a sign-in's `signal` also stops `startMcpSignIn()` while it waits for the refresh lock; a store's `withRefreshLock()` throws `McpRefreshLockBusyError` when another process holds the lock too long, which makes `startMcpSignIn()` skip the refresh, while any other lock failure fails the sign-in. Also added `createMcpAuthProvider()`, which refreshes tokens once across requests and, through `McpOAuthServerStore.withRefreshLock()`, across processes; its `redirectUrl` option names a redirect URI the application signs in with, so tokens from a Client ID Metadata Document that lists only an https callback route can be refreshed. Also added the `refreshOnly` option of `authorizeMcp()`, which refreshes without registering a client or replacing a pending authorization's `state` and PKCE verifier.
- Added helpers that let applications name and configure MCP tools like pi's coding agent, moved from it: `createMcpToolName()` (`mcp__<server>__<tool>`, sanitized, with a hash suffix for long or colliding names) and `mcpNamespace()`; `normalizeMcpInputSchema()`, which makes an input schema an object schema; `limitMcpContent()` and `MCP_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES`, which cut model-facing text over 20KB in the middle and optionally save the full text through a caller's `McpOutputSaver`; and `validateMcpServerConfig()`, which validates one entry of the `mcpServers` configuration shape (stdio, Streamable HTTP, `oauth`, `enabled`, `description`, `timeout`), returns the entry tagged with its transport, and keeps the application's own fields for it to check afterwards. `isMcpServerOverride()` recognizes entries that only override a server defined elsewhere.

import subprocess

files = ["packages/codemode/CHANGELOG.md", "packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md",
         "packages/durable/CHANGELOG.md", "packages/schema/CHANGELOG.md",
         "packages/telemetry/CHANGELOG.md", "packages/mcp/CHANGELOG.md"]

def unreleased_block(lines):
    # content after "## [Unreleased]" up to the next "## [" heading, trailing blanks trimmed
    start = lines.index("## [Unreleased]") + 1
    end = next(i for i in range(start, len(lines)) if lines[i].startswith("## ["))
    block = lines[start:end]
    while block and block[-1] == "":
        block.pop()
    return block

def assemble(fork, up):
    fork = fork.decode().splitlines()
    up = up.decode().splitlines()
    up_unr = unreleased_block(up)
    # fork's [Unreleased] section: heading, then blank, then next "## [" heading
    i = fork.index("## [Unreleased]")
    # find the next "## [" heading
    j = next(k for k in range(i+1, len(fork)) if fork[k].startswith("## ["))
    out = fork[:i] + ["## [Unreleased]"] + up_unr + [""] + fork[j:]
    return out

for f in files:
    fork = subprocess.run(["git", "show", "main:" + f], capture_output=True).stdout
    up = subprocess.run(["git", "show", "upstream/main:" + f], capture_output=True).stdout
    out = assemble(fork, up)
    open(f, "w").write("\n".join(out) + "\n")
    heads = [l for l in out if l.startswith("## ")]
    print(f, "->", " | ".join(heads[:4]), "| conflict markers:", "YES" if "<<<<<<" in "\n".join(out) else "NO")
EOF

4| 5| # hummin 6| 7| A GLM-native terminal coding agent: the [pi agent harness](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) (MIT, by Mario Zechner / earendil-works) retuned for Z.ai's GLM models and [colibri](https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri) local inference. 8| 9| Why a fork: GLM is a first-class citizen here, not a compatibility mode. The provider picker surfaces Z.ai and your local colibri instances first, the default model is GLM, and the whole tool assumes you may be talking to a slow, disk-streaming local model instead of a datacenter. 10| 11| > Based on [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi). All credit for the agent core goes upstream; this fork only curates, extends, and rebrands. License: MIT (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). 12| 13| ## Demo 14| 15| Ornith 1.5 35B (local GGUF via llama.cpp) working through four upstream bugs in hummin's own source. Watch the footer: live **tok/s** next to the context bar - 31 tok/s from a model running on a Mac Mini. 16| 17| ![hummin running Ornith 1.5 35B locally at 31 tok/s](https://github.com/rennf93/hummin/blob/main/docs/assets/demo-ornith.gif) 18| 19| ## Install 20| 21| Install the npm package (recommended - the clone below is only for developing hummin itself): 22| 23| ```bash 24| npm install -g hummin-cli 25| ``` 26| Or from a clone (development only): 27| 28| ```bash 29| git clone https://github.com/rennf93/hummin.git 30| cd hummin 31| npm install 32| npm run build 33| cd packages/coding-agent && npm link # puts `hummin` on your PATH 34| ``` 35| 36| Requires Node >= 22.19. 37| 38| ## Quickstart (Z.ai cloud) 39| 40| ```bash 41| export ZAI_API_KEY=your-key # or run `hummin auth login zai` 42| hummin # interactive TUI; GLM-5.3 is the default suggestion 43| hummin -p "summarize this repo" # oneshot mode 44| ``` 45| 46| GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash and GLM-5.3-highspeed ship in the `zai` provider catalog (1M-token context, reasoning variants mapped to `reasoning_effort`). Pick models with `/model`; set a persistent default with the picker's "set as default" action. 47| 48| ## Features 49| 50| - **Agent teamwork**: sessions message each other across terminals and projects (`agent_send`, `/agents`), share a task board (`/team`), spawn bounded subagents (`task`, `/background` on `ctrl+b`), and run scheduled wake-ups (`/cron`). 51| - **Local fleet**: one provider across all your OpenAI-compatible servers (colibri, llama.cpp, Ollama, ...), health-probed and startable from the model picker, with per-origin serialization and real context windows. 52| - **Integrations**: MCP client (`mcpServers`), TypeScript LSP tools (diagnostics/definition/references/hover), declarative `hooks.json`, `ask_user` questions, DuckDuckGo search and SSRF-guarded fetch, Telegram driving via cc-tg-hub (`TG_HUB=1`). 53| - **Safety**: bash sandboxing (macOS seatbelt / Linux bubblewrap) with `[Sandbox]` in-band blocks, destructive-command advisories (`/bashguard`), loop + budget guardrails, project trust, file checkpoints with `/rewind`. 54| - **Memory**: session distillation into lessons plus a self-curating Obsidian-compatible vault, with hybrid BM25 + embeddings recall injected into every session and searchable on demand. 55| - **Visibility**: `/context` token breakdown with cache-hit ratio, `/cost` with local-served vs cloud split, `/status` + `/doctor` dashboards, two-row statusline (user-definable segments). 56| - **UX**: vim editing mode, grouped command palette, custom statusline segments, fullscreen transcript search, themeable, remote browser control over loopback. 57| 58| ## Local inference (colibri, llama.cpp, ...) 59| 60| The bundled `hummin-local` extension turns every configured OpenAI-compatible server into a fleet citizen: one provider per engine+host (so the picker badge says WHICH engine and WHICH host serves a model), the server's own `/v1/models` as the source of truth for model ids, and no guessed placeholder ids for servers that are down. The engine behind each server does not matter - colibri (MoE streaming), llama.cpp, Ollama all work. Configure the fleet in settings (`fleet.servers`, what `hummin init` writes) or via env; fleet order is preference order.

  4| - **Safety depth** (`hummin-sandbox`, `hummin-bashguard`, `hummin-guardrails`, `hummin-plan`, `hummin-session`, `hummin-sys1`: workspace sandboxing (seatbelt/bubblewrap)

  6| - **Integrations**: MCP client with offline dimming (`hummin-mcp`), TypeScript LSP tools with edit-time diagnostics push (`hummin-lsp`), `hooks.json` (`hummin-hooks`), pa
  7|

vault: /Users/renzof/hummin-vault · 73 entities · 83 lessons

Lessons (5):
Problem: Regenerating package-lock.json on macOS silently dropped `resolved`/`integrity` for hundreds of registry entries (npm optional-deps bug), causing `npm ci` on Linux to fail with missing platform-specific packages like `@rolldown/binding-linux-x64-gnu`.
   Approach: Backfilled the missing `resolved`/`integrity` fields from upstream's lockfile (same versions) and the npm registry for the rest, then regenerated the coding-agent install-lock.
   Gotcha: A lockfile regenerated on macOS can look clean locally yet break Linux CI; after regenerating, verify registry entries still carry `resolved`/`integrity` rather than trusting a green local install.

Problem: After pushing a merge, the session initially didn't check CI, leaving failures (lockfile, nix) undetected until later.
   Approach: Verify post-push CI with `gh run watch` to green before declaring done, and use admin-merge (`gh pr merge`) only for the owner's own review-gated PRs.
   Gotcha: A branch green on its own CI can still be red on main-triggered workflows (scheduled paths, workflow_run triggers) - check the runs fired by the merge push itself, not just the PR checks.

Problem: Release `hummin` v1.2.10 after an upstream sync, ensuring CI is green on the exact released commit before tagging (the 1.2.9 release had shipped off a stale HEAD).
   Approach: Added a green-CI guard inside `release.mjs`, then chained `gh run watch --exit-status` on the pushed SHA before `npm run release:patch`. Mid-cycle a model-data refresh moved HEAD; the guard correctly re-gated on the new commit's CI.
   Gotcha: Any push between watch-start and release invalidates the SHA being watched - the gate must re-read `git rev-parse HEAD` and re-check CI at release time, not trust a previously green run.



Problem: hummin-cli 1.0.3 crashed at startup (`ENOENT dist/modes/interactive/theme/dark.json`) and, once themes were present, every TypeScript extension failed with `Cannot find module 'jiti'`.
Approach: Enumerate everything the bundle reads or resolves from disk at runtime, then make the staging script ship all of it: `dist/modes/interactive/theme`, `dist/modes/interactive/assets`, `dist/core/export-html`, plus the FULL upstream dependency set (`jiti` and `typebox` are require.resolve'd by the extension loader; `@silvia-odwyer/photon-node` backs image paste; the `@earendil-works/*` entries back the jiti aliases extensions import). Fixed in 1.0.4 via `scripts/stage-hummin-cli.mjs` (`npm run stage:hummin-cli`), which self-checks themes/export/bundle before packing.
Gotcha: A slim npm manifest must carry every runtime file read AND every runtime module resolution, not just the JS entry. The bundle resolves jiti/typebox/@earendil-works/* from the INSTALLED package dir (createJiti(import.meta.url)), so missing deps only explode when a user with extensions runs it, never in a bare smoke test; test extension loading with real ~/.hummin extensions before publishing. Also: yanked versions can never be re-published under the same number, and granular npm tokens that bypass 2FA may publish but NOT unpublish (1.0.3 could only be deprecated, not removed). npm dist-tag resolution on this Mac served stale cached packuments (`npm install -g hummin-cli` installed 1.0.2 minutes after 1.0.4 shipped); install explicit versions with `--prefer-online`.


Problem: Ensure a fresh global install actually ships current extensions.
   Approach: Installed `hummin-cli@1.6.1` globally via npm, verified `hummin --version` and the bin symlink target.
   Gotcha: First boot of a new install re-seeds `~/.hummin/agent/extensions/` from the installed package's bundled dir - extension hashes change on first launch; that's expected sync, not corruption, and shouldn't be "fixed".

Author: Renzo Franceschini <45401804+rennf93@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 30 01:22:11 2026 +0100

    Sync upstream pi main (2026-10-29) (#15)
    
    * fix: trust robopipi[bot] in PR gate
    
    * fix(coding-agent): stop macOS shell groups before killing them
    
    Reduce the race where killing a foreground child wakes its shell before the shell is signalled. Keep Linux and Windows termination unchanged and preserve kill fallbacks when stopping fails.
    
    closes #11252
    
    * fix(coding-agent): render system messages in HTML export
    
    Render the leading system message as the system prompt and tool list,
    and later system messages as named section and tool updates. The header
    prompt/tools from agent state remain as a fallback for sessions without
    system entries. CLI --export now shows the prompt and tools too (#3464).
    
    closes #11261
    
    * feat(coding-agent): add messageId and timestamp to markdown transformer context
    
    * feat(coding-agent): add messageId and timestamp to markdown transformer context
    
    * fix(coding-agent): update compaction render test for messageMeta argument
    
    ---------
    
    Co-authored-by: Petr Houška <houskape@gmail.com>
    
    * fix(coding-agent): render HTML export for sessions deeper than the call stack
    
    Replace recursive tree walks in the export template (sortChildren, mapNodes,
    markActive) with iterative traversals, and build getPath with push + reverse.
    
    closes #11225
    
    * fix(coding-agent): preserve pi.exec spawn errors
    
    Fixes #11085
    
    * feat(coding-agent): confirm device-code browser and clipboard actions
    
    Knowing how annoying re-logins in corporate environments can be, I think
    we can open the browser and copy the code to the clipboard (what the user
    asks for) without forcing it upon users (which I assume was the reason
    it was removed in 8f0e9251b9265e73cb85e97b8a190db40c96e57c).
    
    This change adds optional browser opening and code copying during
    device-code login after an additional confirmation (usually Enter).
    It should work for all providers, with an optional opt-out controlled
    by the provider author, not user settings.
    
    Fixes #9282.
    
    * docs(coding-agent): shorten device-code login guidance
    
    * fix(tui,coding-agent): rank contiguous fuzzy matches and search session fields separately
    
    fuzzyMatch scored only the greedy leftmost alignment, so a query could be
    scattered over an earlier unrelated part of the text (opus via "openrouter",
    astra via "radius radius/gpt") and the real match ranked last. It now also
    scores every contiguous occurrence and keeps the best alignment.
    
    /resume matched one concatenated id/name/messages/cwd string. Scattered
    matches in megabytes of message text or in UUIDs were noise, and the
    position penalty buried real hits deep in a transcript. Fields are now
    matched separately: name and cwd fuzzy, id and messages exact only, with no
    position penalty. Ranking is name text, then id/message/cwd text, then
    scattered name/cwd matches. Lowercased message text is cached per session.
    
    closes #11220
    
    * fix(evals): drop autoevals dependency
    
    autoevals@0.3.0 declares engines npm: please-use-pnpm, so every npm install printed an EBADENGINE warning. 0.4.1 removes that but adds a pnpm-enforcing preinstall script. The eval only used the Levenshtein scorer, so inline an equivalent normalized similarity helper instead.

commit 4cf69332c3355c0023982d90650830a66617be60
Author: robopipi[bot] <336283572+robopipi[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 4 09:36:54 2026 +0100

    fix(coding-agent): resize images in queued steering and follow-up messages (#11782)
    
    Images in idle prompts go through `processImage`: they are resized to
    the model's limits, and a coordinate hint is added to the text. Images
    in messages queued while the agent was busy skipped this step. That
    covers `steer()`, `followUp()`, `prompt()` with `streamingBehavior`, and
    RPC `steer`/`follow_up`. Those images were sent and saved at full size.
    For example, a 1200x9000 PNG stayed 1200x9000, which is over Anthropic's
    8000 px limit, and because it is saved in the session it was replayed on
    every later request.

Fixes #11738
    
    Requested by @badlogic
    
    Co-authored-by: triagent <triagent@localhost>

Lessons (5):
Problem: User was alarmed by ~50 "echo probe" bash commands appearing in their session.
   Approach: Reassured with concrete proof (`cron_list` empty, all commands read-only one-liners from the session's own audit) before continuing the work.
   Gotcha: Many small gated echo commands look like background activity to the user; when they ask "what's going on", answer the question first (no edits/commands), show evidence nothing external is running, then resume only after explicit confirmation.

Problem: Auditing the laya bash gate extension for false negatives/positives in write-detection.
   Approach: Found `splitSegments` strips redirects, so the whole-command read-only fast path waved writes like `cat a > b` through before the redirect downgrade ran; fixed by gating the fast path with `!hasWriteRedirect()`. Also added a deterministic safe fast path for test-runner commands (`looksLikeTestRun`) since laya scored the repo's own `./test.sh` P=0.80+ despite rubric saying LOW - the checkpoint can't reliably follow the rubric tail.
   Gotcha: A downgrade/threat-check applied after an early-return fast path silently never runs; audit fast paths for any pattern stripped earlier (redirects, env prefixes).

Problem: Verifying fixes end-to-end while my own session's gate hook still ran the pre-fix module.
   Approach: Live-blocked commands (even `./test.sh`, `cp`) were cleared via the gate's own confirm-marker flow (`# laya-gate: confirmed` appended) after verifying targets; the `cp` needed a repo-relative source path to hit the additive-write fast path. Synced fixes to `~/.hummin/agent/extensions/` after; running sessions only pick extensions up at restart.
   Gotcha: In-session hook changes don't apply until restart - use the gate's marker escape hatch rather than retrying blocked commands; long suites go to background `exec` with exit-code echo since piped test output masks earlier failures.

Problem: Reduce sys1 steer latency without weakening the safety gate.
   Approach: Identified three viable designs: fast single-forward-pass classifier path for steer/gate reads, firing the steer read in parallel and injecting it as a queued message, or a deterministic destructive-marker pre-filter (rm/delete/force/drop). User opted to keep as-is; diagnosis recorded for future work.
   Gotcha: The bash gate remains the last-line guard, so making steering non-blocking doesn't remove the safety net - the gate re-checks at command time regardless of the pre-turn read.

Problem: Expose remote (Linux laptop) proxy/model controls from the macOS menubar.
   Approach: All remote health checks and Start/Stop/Restart run as one-line `/bin/zsh -lc` commands over passwordless ssh (`sudo systemctl` on the target), with results logged to `~/Library/Logs/hummin-menubar-actions.log`.
   Gotcha: The token proxy re-reads its `mode.txt` on every request, so a mode switch (all/strip/off) takes effect on the next call with no restart - verify round-trips by reading the file after writing, and restore the original mode after testing. When a host is asleep, ssh fails fast, which just renders the row as "down".

Lessons (5):
Problem: Understanding and modifying the hummin footer rendering (token stats, git status, extension statuses) in interactive mode.
   Approach: The footer was refactored around `FooterDataProvider` (`core/footer-data-provider.ts`): git branch/status caching, extension statuses, and todo summaries live in the provider; `FooterComponent` (`modes/interactive/components/footer.ts`) reads from it via `ReadonlyFooterDataProvider`.
   Gotcha: `FooterComponent.invalidate()` and `dispose()` are intentional no-ops kept for call-site compatibility - invalidation goes through the provider (`footerDataProvider.invalidate()`, `ctx.footer.invalidate()`), not the component. Custom footers from extensions swap into `footerContainer` via `setExtensionFooter()`, passing the provider to the factory.

Problem: Verify whether "Error executing tool" and related MCP flag claims were accurate before acting on another session's report.
   Approach: Grep the repo for the literal string and for the env var across code, docs (`docs/environment-variables.md`), and CHANGELOG to confirm existence, defaults, and documentation status before answering.
   Gotcha: AGENTS.md rule: verify absence/presence claims by search before asserting them - a feature can be already shipped in a prior release; the reporter couldn't check because the hummin source isn't on the NAS.

Problem: Headless fleet sessions saw MCP tool calls fail with a bare "Error executing tool" while long-running server verbs (10+ min) kept completing server-side; another session claimed it was a hummin bug needing a code change.
   Approach: Trace the timeout path in the hummin repo: `hummin-mcp.ts` sets `MCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` per `tools/call` via `mcp-client.ts`; on timeout the client rejects the call, drops the late response cleanly, and the connection stays up. The knob `HUMMIN_MCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` already exists and is documented, so the fix is an env pin (e.g. `=1800000`), not a patch.
   Gotcha: "Hummin-side root cause" ≠ "hummin code change". Also `resolveTimeoutMs` requires `> 0`, so `0` does not disable the timeout - and the env var is read in the hummin process at extension load, not inherited from `mcpServers[].env`. The opaque log message came from roboco's wrapper, which flattens hummin's detailed timeout error.

Problem: Verifying whether a repo-root scratch file's intentional type error would break the project check.
   Approach: Inspected root `tsconfig.json` `include` before running `npm run check`; the file (repo-root `*.ts`) is outside `scripts/` and `packages/**` globs, so `tsc --noEmit` never sees it and check stays green.
   Gotcha: The same intentional error in `packages/*/test/**/*` (inside `include`) does fail `npm run check` - scratch-file location determines whether the type error is invisible or blocking. LSP diagnostics on the edit path work regardless of tsconfig include.

Problem: `sys1_decide` failed with "clef engine unreachable at 9987" and the error hint suggested restarting the Mac laya instance.
   Approach: Restarting laya did nothing (it was healthy, on port 9989); the real fix was identifying which launchd service actually binds the configured port and kickstarting that one.
   Gotcha: The error message names the wrong service to restart. Map engine name to port from env/settings (`HUMMIN_DECISION_ENGINE=clef` -> clef-mlx plist serves `--port 9987`, laya is 9989, bf16 clef is 9988), then check `launchctl print` + `lsof -i` and restart the service that owns the port.

fix(coding-agent): keep model selector selection when the catalog refresh lands (#11810)

Opening the selector starts a background catalog refresh. When it
finished, the selection jumped back to the current model, or to the top
row with a search query, discarding any browsing done in the meantime.

Pass the selected model into filterModels() so the refresh keeps it
selected by provider and ID. If it is gone, the existing fallback
applies. The index is chosen once and the list is rebuilt once.

Based on #11758.

closes #9109

        if: matrix.name != 'durable' && runner.os == 'macOS'

        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Build the pi-env daemon
        if: matrix.name == 'other'
        run: npm run build:daemon --workspace packages/env

      - name: Test
        env:
          SUITE: ${{ matrix.name }}
        run: |
          if [ "$SUITE" != other ]; then
            npm run test --workspace "packages/$SUITE"
            exit 0
          fi
          # Every other workspace, so new packages are tested without editing this workflow.
          args=()
          for dir in packages/*/; do
            case "$dir" in packages/coding-agent/ | packages/durable/) continue ;; esac
            args+=(--workspace "${dir%/}")
          done
          npm run test:scripts
          npm run test --if-present "${args[@]}"

      - name: Extension load smoke
        run: node scripts/check-extensions-load.mjs
